semantics: applicationPolicy is the governed policy version frozen for this session at start (studio_guided_session_policies -> studio_guided_policy_versions.document->'applicationPolicy'), sent byte-for-byte as stored. It is the ONLY source of the guided worker's application policy; a worker-mounted or server-option applicationPolicy is CONFIGURATION_DENIED at process/server construction (R14), never a wire response.

policyHash = lowercase hex SHA-256 over the canonical-v1 UTF-8 bytes of applicationPolicy exactly as sent. The backend sends studio_guided_session_policies.observation_policy_hash and, before sending, recomputes GuidedContracts.hash(applicationPolicy) and refuses RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE if they differ (defensive; the V19 CHECK makes a mismatch unreachable).

The runner recomputes the hash before the first observation (R14 bindContextPolicy). Mismatch, malformed policy or a different hash than the binding in force -> 409 bridge refusal IDENTITY_MISMATCH. A context without either field -> 409 SCHEMA. Both are definite (ar-2-r14-stops ruling 2).

approvedOrigins (unchanged property) carries the session's scope.approvedOrigins, which from C2b is the governed allowedOrigins (see b14Obligations). Every readGrants[].origin is in allowedOrigins by construction (400 INVALID_POLICY otherwise), so the sanitizer's grant-origin check (observationSanitizer.ts:28) holds.

ObservationReadGrant is a deliberate copy of replay-ipc#/definitions/ReadGrant, not a $ref: a $ref would pull replay-ipc.schema.json into the runner's guided bundle, and replay-ipc's ReadGrant uses anyOf, which the runner validator does not support. Differences, all narrowing: origin uses the session-scope pattern instead of format uri + ^https?://[^/?#]+$; 'at least one of visibleText/controlValue' is if/else instead of anyOf. The checker asserts that every valid ObservationReadGrant fixture is also valid against replay-ipc#/definitions/ReadGrant, so the governed form stays a subset of what replay accepts.

governedDocumentKeySet_DLane.normativeSql_replaces_V19_function:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION studio_guided_policy_document(d jsonb) RETURNS boolean LANGUAGE sql IMMUTABLE AS $$
 SELECT (jsonb_typeof(d)='object'
  AND d ?& ARRAY['schemaVersion','allowedOrigins','applicationPolicy','sideEffectStance','destructiveVocabulary']
  AND d-ARRAY['schemaVersion','allowedOrigins','applicationPolicy','sideEffectStance','destructiveVocabulary']='{}'::jsonb
  AND d->'schemaVersion'='3'::jsonb
  AND octet_length(convert_to(d::text,'UTF8'))<=65536
  AND jsonb_typeof(d->'allowedOrigins')='array' AND jsonb_array_length(d->'allowedOrigins') BETWEEN 1 AND 10
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_array_elements(d->'allowedOrigins') o
   WHERE jsonb_typeof(o)<>'string' OR length(o#>>'{}')>256
    OR (o#>>'{}') !~ '^https?://(?:[a-z0-9.-]+|\[[0-9a-f:]+\])(?::[1-9][0-9]{0,4})?$')
  AND (SELECT count(DISTINCT o) FROM jsonb_array_elements(d->'allowedOrigins') o)=jsonb_array_length(d->'allowedOrigins')
  AND jsonb_typeof(d->'applicationPolicy')='object'
  AND (d->'applicationPolicy') ?& ARRAY['policyRuleId','allowStructuralDiscovery','readGrants']
  AND (d->'applicationPolicy')-ARRAY['policyRuleId','allowStructuralDiscovery','readGrants']='{}'::jsonb
  AND d->'applicationPolicy'->'allowStructuralDiscovery'='true'::jsonb
  AND jsonb_typeof(d->'applicationPolicy'->'readGrants')='array'
  AND jsonb_array_length(d->'applicationPolicy'->'readGrants')<=32
  AND d->>'sideEffectStance' IN ('ALLOW','CLARIFY_FIRST','DENY')
  AND jsonb_typeof(d->'destructiveVocabulary')='array'
  AND jsonb_array_length(d->'destructiveVocabulary') BETWEEN 1 AND 64
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM jsonb_array_elements(d->'destructiveVocabulary') v
   WHERE jsonb_typeof(v)<>'string' OR length(v#>>'{}') NOT BETWEEN 1 AND 64 OR v#>>'{}'<>lower(v#>>'{}'))
  AND (SELECT count(DISTINCT v) FROM jsonb_array_elements(d->'destructiveVocabulary') v)=jsonb_array_length(d->'destructiveVocabulary')
 ) IS TRUE
$$;

        Readable by a principal who may read the CSI, or who is in a configured approver group.
        A caller who may do neither gets `403 STUDIO_FORBIDDEN` before any lookup. `404` is only
        reachable after authorization and means the caller may read this CSI and no policy exists

      parameters:
        - { name: csiId, in: query, required: true, schema: { type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 20 } }
        - { name: applicationId, in: query, required: true, schema: { type: string, minLength: 1, maxLength: 256 } }

      responses:

        not write get the same `403`. `expectedVersion` other than the latest version is
        `409 STALE_REVISION` and writes nothing. Body rules and normalization are those of

          description: Created. The new version is the latest version; the active version is unchanged.

        '403': { $ref: '#/components/responses/Forbidden' }
        '409':
          description: '`expectedVersion` is not the latest version. Nothing is written; reload and retry.'
          x-conflict-codes: [STALE_REVISION]
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse' }

      - { $ref: '#/components/parameters/GuidedPolicyVersion' }

      summary: Record the Security approval of the latest version, which activates it
      x-implemented-by: STUDIO-OBS-014
      description: |
        Only a principal in a configured approver group may approve, and never the principal who
        created that version. With no approver group configured (the default), every approval is
        `403`: the route fails closed. A caller who is not an approver, an unknown id, and the

startGuidedSession.replace409and_add429:
Replace the one-line '409' response of startGuidedSession with the block below and insert '429' after it, verbatim (indentation as in the file, 8 spaces before the status keys):
        '409':
          description: |
            Revision, authorization, state, idempotency or policy conflict; closed v3 `{code}`
            refusal. Nothing is written: no session, no publication base, no budget charge.

            `POLICY_NOT_APPROVED` (STUDIO-OBS-014 AC-1): the application environment has no
            approved governed observation policy, or its latest version is not yet approved
            (an edit awaiting approval blocks new learning even while an older version is active).
            `messageCode` is `GUIDED_POLICY_ABSENT`, `GUIDED_POLICY_UNAPPROVED` or
            `GUIDED_POLICY_PENDING_VERSION`. Not retryable until the policy is approved.

            `RUNTIME_INCOMPATIBLE` includes a governed policy whose origins are no longer all
            trusted by the platform policy for this application environment (re-checked at every
            start; governance can narrow the trusted origins, never widen them).
          content:
            application/json:
              schema: { $ref: '../studio-observed-authoring/contracts/v3/error.schema.json' }
              examples:
                policyNotApproved:
                  value: { schemaVersion: 3, code: POLICY_NOT_APPROVED, messageCode: GUIDED_POLICY_PENDING_VERSION, requestId: sample-request, retryable: false }
        '429':
          description: |
            Budget refusal. Two producers share this status (same pattern as ADR-002 §31):

            - The Studio handler's v3 error `BUDGET_EXCEEDED`. `retryable: true` with messageCode
              `CSI_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS_EXHAUSTED` or `CSI_DAILY_TOKENS_EXHAUSTED` is the per-CSI
              budget (STUDIO-OBS-014 AC-8) and always carries `Retry-After`. `retryable: false` is a
              per-session bound (for example too many source steps) that no wait resolves, and
              carries no `Retry-After`.
            - The platform rate-limit filter's `RATE_LIMITED` (start is metered as `EXECUTE`),
              in the platform envelope, always with `Retry-After`.
          headers:
            Retry-After:
              description: |
                Whole seconds, at least 1. Daily token budget: seconds until the next UTC midnight
                on the database clock. Concurrent sessions: seconds until the earliest live session
                of the CSI reaches its hard expiry, an upper bound on when a slot frees. Absent on a
                non-retryable per-session bound.
              schema: { type: integer, minimum: 1 }
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                oneOf:
                  - { $ref: '../studio-observed-authoring/contracts/v3/error.schema.json' }
                  - { $ref: '#/components/schemas/PlatformErrorResponse' }
              examples:
                csiConcurrentSessions:
                  value: { schemaVersion: 3, code: BUDGET_EXCEEDED, messageCode: CSI_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS_EXHAUSTED, requestId: sample-request, retryable: true }
                csiDailyTokens:
                  value: { schemaVersion: 3, code: BUDGET_EXCEEDED, messageCode: CSI_DAILY_TOKENS_EXHAUSTED, requestId: sample-request, retryable: true }
                rateLimited:
                  value: { error: { code: RATE_LIMITED, message: Rate limit exceeded } }

readmeCanonicalRule.contractsReadme:
Insert as a new paragraph directly before the paragraph that begins "The replay family (`replay-*`, `publication`, `revision`)", verbatim:

Canonical-v1 string escaping is normative and equals ECMAScript `JSON.stringify` (RFC 8785 §3.2.2.2): `\"` and `\\`; the short escapes `\b`, `\t`, `\n`, `\f`, `\r`; every other code point U+0000–U+001F as `\u00` followed by two **lowercase** hexadecimal digits (U+001F is `\u001f`, never `\u001F`); nothing else is escaped — not `/`, not U+007F, not U+2028/U+2029, not any non-ASCII scalar, which is written as raw UTF-8. Unpaired surrogates are refused before serialisation. The `c0-controls` vector in `publication-canonical-vectors.json` and every `observationPolicyHashVectors` entry in `fixtures.json` pin this; Java (`GuidedContracts`), Node (`contracts.hash` and the other runner canonicalizers) and PostgreSQL (`studio_publication_canonical`) must each reproduce them independently.
readmeCanonicalRule.publicationContractsMd_line11: In docs/specs/studio-observed-authoring/publication-contracts.md:11 replace "ordinary JSON escaping (quote/backslash/control characters; no escape of non-ASCII or slash)" with "JSON escaping exactly as ECMAScript `JSON.stringify` / RFC 8785 §3.2.2.2 (quote, backslash, the short escapes `\b \t \n \f \r`, other U+0000–U+001F as `\u00xx` with lowercase hex; no escape of slash, U+007F, U+2028/U+2029 or non-ASCII; see contracts/README.md)". This is a clarification of the existing rule, not a change: 'Canonical-v1 remains unchanged' stays true.
readmeCanonicalRule.governedPolicyParagraph:
Add to contracts/README.md after the bridge Status-mapping paragraph (and after the refusal sentence above), verbatim:

Governed observation policy (STUDIO-OBS-014 AC-1). `runner-context.applicationPolicy` is the approved governed policy version frozen for the session at start, sent byte-for-byte as stored, and `policyHash` is the canonical-v1 SHA-256 of exactly that object. The worker recomputes it before the first observation and refuses a mismatch with `IDENTITY_MISMATCH`; a later context of the same session cannot change the policy in force. A worker-mounted `applicationPolicy` is `CONFIGURATION_DENIED` at start-up. The governed document (`guided-policy.schema.json#/definitions/policyDocument`) is stored normalized: omitted `sideEffectStance` = `CLARIFY_FIRST`, omitted `destructiveVocabulary` = the configured baseline, `allowedOrigins` and `destructiveVocabulary` sorted by code point, `readGrants` sorted by `policyRuleId`, `controlValue.types` in enum order. The session's `approvedOrigins` are the governed `allowedOrigins`, which must stay within the platform-trusted origins. Replay is unaffected: it keeps its published snapshot and the configured platform policy.
